why: The race explorer against its own refactors (design/race-pure.md). Four async units of one shape and one async method (a query, a Map of aliases built in a loop, awaits in a loop over a query result, a report written at the end), on a module with a value import, so every pair of events is dependent and each side's order set is cut by the bound. bindPure adds one pure local (const aliasCount = aliases.size), bindMoved moves a pure computation (the label) across two awaits, bindUntouched is the same text on both sides: each is PASS-bounded, with 28 orders per side over 2 programs, 3 prefixes cut, 12 drawn orders (lane B at n 30). Before this reading all four were ASK, the untouched one included: the drawn orders differed per side, and the library recorder's reads of a fake entered one side's trace only. bindAwaitOrder asks the two queries together and awaits them in turn, where the parent asks the second after the first answers: the same requests in the same order on one call, but the parent alone lets the second caller's first query fall between its two, and the candidate's order set is cut, so it is ASK naming one interleaving per side (the candidate's arm order, and the parent's arm order, since the candidate's order is not feasible on the parent). DeleteAgentUseCase.execute is a use case on a receiver (four awaited ports, a cache eviction in a try) whose two sides differ by one comment only, a corpus unit made self-contained (its ports in api.d.ts): before this reading lane B asked (program 1, a drawn order the parent alone ran), now PASS-bounded with 22 orders per side over 2 programs, 1 cut per side, 12 drawn. Lane A refuses every unit by design (a push on the result of Map.get is alias-mutation; the use case's file imports an unresolved framework module), so the pair checks lane B alone (laneBOnly).
